composition.story: One new sample goes to all five trees. Each tree, trained on a different random sample of the data, gives its own answer. The forest then combines them: classification takes a majority vote, regression takes the average. Step through the votes, then switch the task to compare the two rules.

aha.observation: The forest does not pick one tree. It counts all five answers, so Cat wins 3 to 2 and the two Dog trees are outvoted.

controls.label: Task (combining rule)
controls.presentation: Switches the combining rule applied to the same five trees.

states.label: Send x
states.sentence: The same new sample x is sent to all five trees. No tree has answered yet.
states.why: Every tree sees the same input.

states.label: Tree 1 votes
states.sentence: Tree 1 follows its own splits and votes Cat.
states.why: Each tree answers alone, from its own splits.

states.label: Tree 2 votes
states.sentence: Tree 2 was trained on a different random sample. It disagrees and votes Dog.
states.why: Different training samples give different answers.

states.label: Tree 3 votes
states.sentence: Tree 3 votes Cat. Cat now leads by one vote.
states.why: Votes are counted as they arrive.

states.label: Tree 4 votes
states.sentence: Tree 4 votes Cat. Cat has 3 votes, and 3 is already a majority of 5.
states.why: A majority is more than half of the trees.

states.label: Tree 5 votes
states.sentence: Tree 5 votes Dog. All five trees have now answered, and they do not agree.
states.why: The trees are not forced to agree.

states.label: Tally votes
states.sentence: The combiner counts every vote per class: Cat 3, Dog 2. Share of Cat is 3/5 = 60%.
states.why: The tally is the combining step.

states.label: Forest answer
states.sentence: The class with the most votes wins. The forest answers Cat, and the two Dog trees are outvoted.

states.sentence: Tree 1 predicts the number 12 for x.
states.why: Each tree gives a number, not a class.

states.label: Tree 2 predicts
states.sentence: Tree 2 predicts 15. Different training samples give different numbers.
states.why: The trees spread around a typical value.

states.label: Tree 3 predicts
states.sentence: Tree 3 predicts 11, the lowest so far.
states.why: Values are added as they arrive.

states.label: Tree 4 predicts
states.why: Four of five values are in.

states.label: Tree 5 predicts
states.sentence: Tree 5 predicts 13. All five values are in, ranging from 11 to 15.
states.why: The trees disagree by up to 4.

states.label: Average
states.sentence: The combiner divides the sum by the number of trees: 65 / 5 = 13.

states.label: Forest answer
states.sentence: The forest answers 13, the mean of all five trees. No single tree is chosen.
